## Join the Lab

We welcome students and researchers who want to combine psychology with computational and quantitative methods. Pick the path that fits you.

::: {.opp-card .opp-ug}
::: {.opp-side}
### Undergraduate Students

Learn research by doing it, earn credit, and build toward a thesis.

```{=html}
<div class="btns"><a class="primary" href="mailto:jmgirard@ku.edu">Apply to be a research assistant</a></div>
```
:::
::: {.opp-body}
The lab is frequently home to undergraduate students from Psychology and Behavioral Neuroscience, and occasionally from other departments.

Research assistants learn the scientific method and help collect and process research data. Many enroll in PSYC 480 for **credit hours**. Assistants attend weekly lab meetings and can expect a **letter of recommendation** describing their contributions (please give one month of notice). Advanced assistants are sometimes offered **co-authorship** on research products such as conference presentations.

Honors students can design and complete an **honors thesis** under Dr. Girard's supervision during their senior year. These students typically apply for, and have often won, **research awards** from the [Center for Undergraduate Research](https://ugresearch.ku.edu/) and **present** their work at the [Undergraduate Research Symposium](https://ugresearch.ku.edu/student/share/symposium).
:::
:::

::: {.opp-card .opp-grad}
::: {.opp-side}
### Prospective Graduate Students

Doctoral training in the BBQ and CPS concentrations.

```{=html}
<div class="btns"><a class="primary" href="https://psychology.ku.edu/psychology-graduate-program">Learn about graduate admissions</a></div>
```
:::
::: {.opp-body}
The [KU Psychology Department](https://psychology.ku.edu/psychology-graduate-program) grants doctoral degrees (**PhDs**) in three concentrations: Brain, Behavior, and Quantitative Science (BBQ); Clinical Psychological Science (CPS); and Social Psychology. The department does not offer a terminal master's degree, and the CPS concentration focuses on adult rather than child psychopathology.

Dr. Girard advises students in the **BBQ** and **CPS** concentrations and is an especially good match for students whose interests span both, such as CPS students interested in advanced methods or BBQ students interested in medical applications.

Graduate students complete coursework in the department and conduct research in the lab, with many opportunities to contribute to ongoing projects. Information about each admissions cycle appears on the [News](news.qmd) page.
:::
:::

::: {.opp-card .opp-post}
::: {.opp-side}
